plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: Gnarled branches, still bare of leaves, burst into clouds of delicately scented blossoms. The flowers open while late-winter chill lingers, and their sweet, spicy fragrance drifts through gardens and orchards. They are a beloved herald of spring.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late January to mid-March, often peaking in late February and early March
plants.location: Japan, including the orchards and shrine gardens of Honshu, plus eastern China and Korea
plants.funFact: Ume blossoms have been celebrated in East Asian poetry and art for well over a thousand years. Their fruit is pickled into umeboshi and steeped into plum wine.

plants.name: Narcissus pseudonarcissus
plants.description: Wild daffodils light up woodlands and meadows with nodding, golden trumpets framed by paler petals. They carpet the ground in drifts of yellow, a cheerful sign that winter is loosening its grip.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late February through March, with March 10 falling within the typical peak in many areas
plants.location: Western Europe, including the woodlands and meadows of England, Wales and France
plants.funFact: All parts of the daffodil contain toxic alkaloids. One of them, galantamine, was first studied from related bulbs and is now used in medicine.

plants.name: Eschscholzia californica
plants.description: Silky, cup-shaped blooms in glowing orange cover hillsides and roadsides. The petals open in full sun and fold closed on cloudy days and at night, so whole slopes seem to switch on and off with the light.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter through spring, with early blooms appearing in March in warm years, especially after winter rains
plants.location: California, USA, including the Central Valley foothills and southern deserts and grasslands
plants.funFact: It is the official state flower of California. Its petals close at night and in cool, cloudy weather.
